In the end, the Buchanan ''peasants,'' as Patrick Buchanan likes to call his delegates, went to San Diego, and, like the proverbial disappointed tourist, all they got was this lousy pro-life plank.

 Their man was banned from the podium, Dole floor managers quashed their plan for a quiet walkout during Representative Susan Molinari's keynote speech, and party leaders fought their efforts to abstain on the first ballot. They couldn't even waive a Buchanan poster without a Dole loyalist blocking them from camera view. ''We have no voice,'' Mike Flory, a Buchanan delegate from Michigan, said woefully. ''We are outside the castle with no way to cross the moat. We have no choice.''

nytimes_articles.headline: Sand-Castle Mentality on Fire Island
nytimes_articles.abstract:
Thanks to the inevitable effects of a rising sea level, 80 to 90 percent of American ocean shoreline is retreating inland. This is nature's course, and it is not really a problem unless buildings are threatened.

 Fire Island has both houses and a retreating shoreline. The result is what property owners call beach ''erosion,'' whereby the advancing surf appears to gobble up the sand that forms a protective buffer for beachfront homes. The Army Corps of Engineers wants to help owners by bringing in new sand, thus ''replenishing'' the threatened beaches. But replenishment always comes at a price.

nytimes_articles.abstract: Alex J Mandl, AT&T's president and presumed heir to chairman and chief executive, resigns to run tiny start-up company; Mandl's departure is another rude shock during turbulent year for AT&T; company has been badly criticized for laying off 40,000 employees after splitting into three companies; in addition, AT&T's long-distance business is eroding; Robert E Allen, AT&T's chairman, says he will look outside AT&T for new president; during interim, he will run company along with Richard W Miller, chief financial officer, and John D Zeglis, senior executive vice president; AT&T stock plummets following announcement of Mandl's resignation; Mandl will become chairman of Associated Communications, company that owns licenses to offer variety of wireless telephone and data services; he is said to be getting $20 million signing bonus, plus 18 percent equity stake; Associated Communications is owned by investor Myles P Berkman; it is 'fixed wireless' provider--a wireless version of local phone company, for business customers that want high-capacity networks without stringing huge cables; it is new type of wireless technology that is promising, but utterly unproved; photo (L)
